persona: Music fan new to music production; wanted a short dance groove
evaluation_type: Independent simulated beginner; not a real human study
method: Visible native UI and screenshots only. All composition, edits, playback, saving and exporting used mouse clicks, double-clicks, drags or scroll. No keyboard, source inspection or state injection.

completion.composition: 14 bars at 112 BPM; manually drawn C4, D#4, G4, A#4 short notes per bar; stock Circuit rhythm audio repeated and final clip trimmed.
completion.playback_evidence: Both track meters moved while transport advanced; null audio output prevents listening.

ratings_scale: 1 to 5, higher means more of the named property; high confusion is worse

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible double-click MIDI hint, pencil notes, context Duplicate and File export supported completion. Precise length and tempo editing needed exploration.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Clean restrained dark palette, clear waveforms and note previews feel modern. Much empty space and muted controls make the starting surface a little austere.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most click feedback and note edits felt immediate in screenshot evidence. First usable MIDI pattern appeared in under a minute. Export finished within the subsequent short interaction sequence. This is perceived workflow speed, not benchmarked latency.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Toolbar controls moved when changing tools; tempo appeared text-only; there was no discoverable zoom-out control; source preview failure could look like a broken instrument.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The requested audio, piano-roll, VST3, duplication, trimming, save, WAV and MIDI workflows worked. Mouse-only tempo/renaming and easy precise duration controls were missing or undiscovered. Lab catalogue offered only one instrument, so sound-library breadth and third-party compatibility cannot be rated.

findings.title: Tool selection rearranges controls and causes misclicks
findings.observed: Switching Select to Pencil moved Length from the left of row 2 to the right of row 1. Clicking its former position opened Grid scale settings.
findings.recommendation: Keep shared controls in stable positions across tools; reserve a predictable slot for tool-specific controls.

findings.title: Tempo has no discoverable mouse adjustment
findings.observed: Clicking 112.0 BPM selected a text input. Scrolling 16 steps did not change it. No +/- buttons or drag hint appeared.
findings.recommendation: Add visible decrement/increment controls or documented drag adjustment with precise value feedback.

findings.title: Exact duration requires export-dialog checking and tiny edge corrections
findings.observed: Trimming to the visible 0:30.00 ruler point produced 30.134 seconds. A 4 px correction did nothing; switching Snap to 1/4 and a larger trim gave exactly 30.000.
findings.recommendation: Show clip start/end/duration while trimming and provide mouse-friendly duration/range controls; offer bar snap.

findings.title: Zoom out was not discoverable
findings.observed: View menu offered Fit selection and waveform amplitude but no visible zoom out. Scrolling the ruler did not change scale. Fit solved the immediate problem after duplication.
findings.recommendation: Expose small zoom-in/out controls adjacent to Fit, with tooltips.

findings.title: Preview failure is easy to confuse with plugin failure
findings.observed: Library showed Preview failed 1 and Preview Failed for the only instrument, yet assignment and MIDI channel activity worked.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish unavailable preview artwork from an instrument load failure; use actionable status text.

positive_findings: The empty area clearly said Double-click for MIDI and opened the correct instrument chooser.
Assign instrument action was visible and returned directly to a ready pattern.
Pencil drag length and note labels made the first pattern straightforward.
Marquee selection plus context Duplicate expanded both audio and MIDI reliably.
Native save/export dialogs supplied filenames, allowing mouse-only output without naming friction.
Export summary displayed exact arrangement duration and completion banner offered Copy path.
limits: Simulated beginner feedback, not human research.
Null audio device means no listening evaluation or sound-quality claim.
Only lab sine VST3 was available; no third-party VST validation.
The piece reused stock audio; it did not test audio import or recording.
No professional mixing, effects or automation workflow tested.
